previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 25%), ICD, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure was admitted for acute kidney injury following a recent hospitalization for heart failure exacerbation. He presented with elevated creatinine (3.2 mg/dL), dizziness on standing, and episodes of chest burning with weakness. Evaluation revealed hypovolemia and overdiuresis due to recent initiation of torsemide and spironolactone, leading to acute on chronic renal failure. He also experienced symptomatic PVCs causing transient hypoperfusion, managed by increasing metoprolol to 75 mg daily. The warfarin dose was increased to 5 mg daily for subtherapeutic INR, with heparin bridging. Renal function improved with IV hydration and holding nephrotoxic medications. He was discharged on reduced torsemide (10 mg daily), continued amiodarone, and new metoprolol dose, with plans to restart spironolactone and lisinopril outpatient. Follow-up was arranged for labs, vascular surgery, and EP device check.
